notes: Measures of the Board of Supervisors at a numbered address, 1926-1945, other than the garage and filling-station permits (board-permits-1926-1931): the city's leases of buildings and floors for public use (library reading rooms, WPA and NYA projects, wartime civil defence and teen-age centres), sales of city-owned buildings for removal ahead of street openings, The Emporium's bridge and subway across Jessie Street, the municipal kitchen for the unemployed, and the federal buildings listed in the Mayor's annual report for 1942. Found by a scan of measure titles carrying a street number (/mnt/project-files/sf-supervisors-journal/early/titles.py), then read one by one. Nuisance-abatement resolutions (bare declarations with no description of the premises) and lists of names and addresses were left out. Lessors who are individuals are left out.

coverage.remaining: Titles not ending in a period, or set in capitals, were not caught by the scan; vols 3-20 (1908-1925) are not on the Internet Archive.

raw.text: Rooms Nos. 407 and 408 in the Western Women's Club Building at 609 Sutter Street ... The premises are required by the San Francisco Civilian War Council

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 609 SUTTER ST → parcel 0297001; sf-parcels has blklot 0297001 active, 535–535 MASON; the 2025 roll records it as commercial misc, built 1927. EAS puts 601, 609 SUTTER ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 601.

findings.description: The Board renewed, for the Recreation Commission, the city's lease of the second floor and parts of the first floor and basement here, held since February 1, 1944.

citation.label: Journal of Proceedings, Board of Supervisors of the City and County of San Francisco, January 22, 1945

raw.text: covering the second floor, 300 square feet of the first floor comprising the entrance, and 1000 square feet in the basement in that certain building known as No. 1441 Van Ness Avenue ... the Recreation Commission desires that said lease be renewed

resolution.method: No record in sf-eas-addresses for 1441 VAN NESS AVE.
resolution.note: The address does not exist today, so there is no page it can go on. The nearest surviving numbers on the street are 1430, 1450, 1455. Per "The evidence bar" in research/AGENTS.md this is a street-hub fact: a dated record of a building at a number the city no longer has.

findings.description: The Board authorized a month-to-month lease of top-floor space here, from February 1, 1945, for a Recreation Department teen-age center.

citation.label: Journal of Proceedings, Board of Supervisors of the City and County of San Francisco, January 22, 1945

raw.text: certain top floor space in the building located at 107 Sagamore Street ... Said premises are required by the Recreation Department for a Teen-age Center

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 107 SAGAMORE ST → parcel 7147032; sf-parcels has blklot 7147032 active, 103–107 SAGAMORE; the 2025 roll records it as commercial retail, built 1929. EAS puts 103, 105, 107 SAGAMORE ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 103.

findings.description: The Board authorized the sale at auction, for removal within thirty days, of the city-owned dwelling house here, on land acquired for the extension of Mount Vernon Avenue.

citation.label: Journal of Proceedings, Board of Supervisors of the City and County of San Francisco, July 12, 1926

raw.text: Dwelling house and appurtenances situated on that certain piece or parcel of land acquired for the extension of Mt. Vernon avenue, and known as No. 60 Harold avenue

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 60 HAROLD AVE → parcel 6978023; sf-parcels has blklot 6978023 active, 60–60 HAROLD; the 2025 roll records it as single family residential, built 1947.
resolution.note: The house stood on land acquired for the extension of Mount Vernon Avenue and was sold for removal; the roll dates the building now at 60 Harold Avenue to 1947, and the house's lot may now be street. Not placed.

findings.address_as_written: No. 59 Merritt street and No. 61 Merritt street
findings.description: The Board authorized the sale at auction, for removal within thirty days, of the city-owned dwelling houses at 59 and 61 Merritt Street, on land acquired for the extension of Market Street.

citation.label: Journal of Proceedings, Board of Supervisors of the City and County of San Francisco, July 12, 1926

raw.text: Dwelling houses and appurtenances situated on those certain pieces or parcels of land acquired for the extension of Market street, and known as No. 59 Merritt street and No. 61 Merritt street

resolution.method: sf-eas-addresses holds no street named MERRITT ST, under that spelling or any spelling of it, so the address cannot be looked up.
resolution.note: The street the record names is not a street in the city's address registry today; the record may name a private way, a renamed street or a spelling this pass could not match.
